sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Pullover Machine is an isolation exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi through a fixed arc of motion using arm pads or handles.

The lifter sits on the machine and pushes the arms down and away, contracting the lats while keeping the torso stationary.

Unlike free weight pullovers, the machine provides constant tension throughout the range of motion and removes balance demands, making it an excellent hypertrophy tool for the lats.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Direct isolation of the latissimus dorsi
- Constant tension throughout the range of motion
- Reduced lower back demand compared to free weight pullovers
- Easy to load progressively on the weight stack
- Reinforces the mind-muscle connection with the lats
- Strong stretch position challenges the lats deeply
- Excellent accessory for pull-ups and rows

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Latissimus Dorsi

Secondary: Pectoralis Major, Teres Major, Long Head of Triceps, Core

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Adjust the seat of the plate-loaded pullover machine so that when you sit, your upper arms align with the machine's arm pads.
2. Load the machine with an appropriate weight.
3. Confirm the seat is locked in position before starting.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Sit on the machine and secure your upper arms under the pads.
2. Grasp the handles if available.
3. Keep your back flat against the seat and plant your feet firmly on the ground for stability.

sections.heading: Pull Down
sections.content:
1. Inhale and, using a controlled motion, push the machine's arms down and away from you.
2. Extend your arms fully along the resistance arc.
3. Your torso should remain stationary, with the movement coming from your shoulders and lats.

sections.heading: Return and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Exhale as you slowly return to the starting position.
2. Bring the machine's arms back up with a controlled motion.
3. Focus on feeling the stretch in your lats and chest. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Using momentum or jerking the weight
- Letting the torso lean forward to lift more weight
- Cutting the range of motion short
- Failing to control the eccentric portion
- Squeezing the elbow pads too tightly
- Holding the breath through the rep
- Selecting too heavy a load and losing form

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Plate-loaded pullover machine
- Weight plates
- Athletic shoes for foot traction
- Optional: Mirror to monitor form

sections.heading: Machine Adjustments
sections.content:
1. Adjust the seat height so the upper arms align with the arm pads.
2. Confirm the seat belt or lap pad (if equipped) is set comfortably.
3. Load the machine with an appropriate weight.
4. Confirm the locking pin is fully engaged before starting.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than hip-width.
2. Torso: Pressed firmly into the seat back, ribs stacked, core braced.
3. Arms: Upper arms pressed into the pads, elbows pointing forward.
4. Hands: Lightly gripping the handles if available.
5. Head: Neutral, eyes forward.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Dumbbell Pullover: Free weight pullover on a bench
- Cable Straight Arm Pulldown: Cable lat isolation
- Lat Pulldown: Vertical pulling for lats
- Pull Up: Bodyweight vertical pull
- Barbell Pullover: Barbell version of the free weight pullover
- Single Arm Cable Pullover: Unilateral cable variation

sections.heading: Pullover Machine Variations
sections.content:
Standard Pullover Machine: Described here
Single Arm Pullover Machine: One arm at a time for unilateral focus
Neutral Grip Pullover Machine: Uses neutral handles for shoulder comfort
Wide Grip Pullover Machine: Wider grip for upper lat emphasis
Paused Pullover Machine: Pause at full stretch for greater lat tension
Tempo Pullover Machine: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Pain: Reduce range of motion at the stretched position
Low Back Pain: Keep the back firmly pressed into the seat
Elbow Pain: Use a lighter load and avoid locking out aggressively
No Machine Access: Use cable straight arm pulldowns or dumbbell pullovers
Beginners: Start light to learn the movement before progressing
Limited Mobility: Reduce range of motion to a comfortable level
